research_question: Why does full mean removal improve retrieval while harming radial hierarchy order, and which mean-error direction components affect these outcomes?
conclusion: Radial mean removal harms direct parent order in both fixed models. Orthogonal tangent mean removal improves micro MRR in both, but no hierarchy improvement passes the complete18 Holm family. Direct R-T parent-order comparisons favor T in both; direct R-T MRR favors T significantly only in model11.

condition_definitions.R: remove radial component of independently calibrated mean at fixed full-output p
condition_definitions.T: remove orthogonal tangent component of that mean at fixed p

limitations: Previously observed evaluation samples reused: exploratory mechanism evidence, not a new independent confirmation set.
Two fixed models on one dataset; conditional intervals omit calibration and training-population uncertainty.
Radial order about fixed p[root] is a hierarchy proxy. Neither radius change nor MRR improvement alone establishes semantic hierarchy recovery.
No significant T-S hierarchy difference is not evidence of noninferiority or proof that hierarchy is unchanged.
R and T are local tangent components. Finite effects need not add to O and T may change global radius.
R/T use unavailable full p and independent calibration; they are diagnostics, not deployable sampling-only modules.
Current GNNs remain weaker than the earlier bounded text MLP; backbone competitiveness is unresolved.
next_action: Stop new experimental work after current A/B delivery; discuss results and next concrete design with user before continuing.
